question:
We are planning a project that depends on a third-party API nobody on the team has used and on a performance target we may not be able to reach. How should we handle these things that could go wrong, both when planning the work and while it is under way?

Answer with a list of guidelines. After each guideline, cite the source it comes from: the path of the SWEBOK file if you have it, otherwise a verbatim quote of at least 8 words from the passage, in the form (source: ...).
answer:
# Summary

When a project depends on an unfamiliar third-party API or a potentially unreachable performance target, teams should identify these as risks early, analyze their probability and impact, build mitigation strategies, prototype or simulate to validate feasibility, monitor risks continuously throughout the project, and document all decisions so the team can adapt when reality diverges from the plan.

# Guidelines

- Identify risk factors, analyze the probability and potential impact of each, prioritize them, and develop [SWEBOK excerpt 865049d7f34c4858ec74] minimize its impact if it materializes; record everything in a risk register. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Risk Management and Quality Assessment/Risk Management_ Identification, Analysis, and Mitigation Strategies.md)

- Perform risk management [SWEBOK excerpt 3f32cf09481746d60739]. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Risk Management and Quality Assessment/Continuous Risk and Quality Management/Risk Management Throughout Project Life Cycle.md)

- Use risk assessment methods such as [SWEBOK excerpt bb228fe333a5104c91f2] to identify and evaluate risk factors; also determine project abandonment conditions with all relevant stakeholders. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Risk Management and Quality Assessment/Risk Assessment Methods and Software Project Risk Management.md)

- Use [SWEBOK excerpt e670343669547c2ffe2b] use Monte Carlo simulation tools [SWEBOK excerpt 01a6adbf290e70d58033] combining multiple input probability distributions. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Engineering Processes and Quality Assurance/Software Engineering Processes, Lifecycles, and Measurement/Data Collection, Quality Assurance, and Project Monitoring/Project Tracking and Risk Management Tools.md)

- Apply a risk-driven approach to architecture: [SWEBOK excerpt 763761c826bb89b37552], whether those risks result from a small solution space, extremely demanding quality requirements, or possible high-risk failures. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Foundations of Software Architecture/Software Architecture Foundations and Design Principles/Software Architecture_ Foundations, Methods, and Modern Practice/Risk-Driven Software Architecture Approach.md)

- Use prototyping to try out the least-understood software aspects or components first, as this contrasts with methods that begin with the best-understood portions and helps surface unknowns early. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Engineering Processes and Quality Assurance/Formal Methods, Agile Development, and Software Quality/Verification and Prototyping Approaches/Prototyping Methods in Software Engineering.md)

- Use prototypes to concretely demonstrate important dimensions of an implementation, expose engineers' assumptions, and obtain useful feedback; [SWEBOK excerpt 786472a44a8cccda297d]. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Requirements Validation and Management/Prototyping for Requirements Validation and Feedback.md)

- Use formal design analysis with mathematical models to predict [SWEBOK excerpt 077c58c460231685de5d], and use simulation and feasibility prototypes as [SWEBOK excerpt 72c38f59828954d960f1] through performance simulation. - Ensure performance requirements are testable and quantified so compliance or noncompliance can be clearly demonstrated, and verify that requirements are feasible — that [SWEBOK excerpt 1f1c1333967b74fab0f5]. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Requirements_ Foundations and Engineering Practices/Requirements Engineering_ Elicitation, Analysis, and Specification/Requirements Analysis and Refinement/Software Requirements Properties and Quality Criteria.md)

- Understand that a quantified performance requirement point is often arbitrary; even if the software cannot fully achieve the stated requirement point, it typically still has value, and the ability to exceed it can significantly increase value in some cases. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Requirements_ Foundations and Engineering Practices/Requirements Engineering_ Elicitation, Analysis, and Specification/Requirements Engineering_ Viability, Verification, and Stakeholder Management/Performance Thresholds and Cost-Effective Quality Optimization/Fail Point and Performance Requirements in Software Systems.md)

- When scope, cost, schedule, or staffing constraints conflict, either reduce scope by removing lowest-priority requirements, increase capacity, or negotiate an appropriate combination; where possible, make scope matching quantitative rather than qualitative. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Requirements Validation and Management/Requirements Management and Prioritization Strategy/Requirements Scope and Prioritization/Scope Matching and Requirements Management.md)

- When acquiring third-party software components, verify [SWEBOK excerpt b3a7cf59bc0d0a7639a0] with architectural design and requirements; integrate the components and verify correctness; and validate [SWEBOK excerpt 187243ef7157884fdd70] in their intended operating environment. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Quality Management and Project Oversight/Software Acquisition and Project Oversight/Software Acquisition and Supplier Contract Management.md)

- Assess adherence to scope, project plan, and related plans continually and at predetermined intervals; revisit the project risk profile regularly; and evaluate adherence to software quality requirements. - Recalculate risk exposures regularly and enable problem detection based on thresholds that have been exceeded; report outcomes when thresholds are exceeded, including timely identification, mitigation, and resolution of issues. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Quality Management and Project Oversight/Software Acquisition and Project Oversight/Risk Monitoring and Control Management/Risk Exposure Recalculation and Threshold Monitoring.md)

- Use project monitoring activities as the basis for decision-making; where [SWEBOK excerpt b8b6e128d8ffb0e3df2f], make changes to the project — for example, in the form of corrective action such as retesting certain software components. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Quality Management and Project Oversight/Software Acquisition and Project Oversight/Risk Monitoring and Control Management/Project Monitoring and Risk-Based Decision Making.md)

- When unanticipated events occur, consider incorporating additional actions such as prototyping to assist in validation, and revise the project plan and other project documents accordingly; in all cases, [SWEBOK excerpt 1de99a76c2dac5f3a4bf]. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Quality Management and Project Oversight/Software Acquisition and Project Oversight/Risk Monitoring and Control Management/Software Project Control and Configuration Management.md)

- Conduct technical reviews to ensure the system can proceed into each design stage with acceptable risk and that all functional and performance requirements [SWEBOK excerpt 2b4629a8b271ab67b961], schedule, risk, and other constraints. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Engineering Processes and Quality Assurance/Software Quality Assurance and Verification Standards/Quality Assurance Reviews and Implementation Practices/Technical Reviews and Audits in Project Management.md)

- Document architectural decisions along with the rationale, assumptions, alternatives considered, and trade-offs used; also record rejected decisions and the reasons for rejection, as this can prevent the project from repeating a poor decision or allow revisiting a decision when conditions have changed. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Foundations of Software Architecture/Software Architecture_ Foundations, Views, and Patterns/Architectural Design Languages, Decisions, and Technical Debt/Documenting Architectural Decisions and Their Rationale.md)

- Conduct a project retrospective analysis [SWEBOK excerpt 1fcd2e4b5300383cd5ac]; draw lessons learned and feed them into organizational learning and improvement endeavors. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Quality Management and Project Oversight/Software Measurement and Organizational Learning/Software Engineering Measurement and Organizational Learning.md)

- Incorporate [SWEBOK excerpt dfb53af98c247d088046] to help improve product quality; risk management can [SWEBOK excerpt f567f49e96e9f6c2dd4e].
